scenes.event: Ava and her family meet for coffee to discuss her mental health.
scenes.description: The family has gathered in a quiet corner of a local coffee shop for a private conversation. Ava sits at the center, her posture tense and guarded. Her mother, Lora, sits across from her, looking concerned and determined. Amy, her younger sister, sits beside Ava, trying to ease the tension.

characters.name: Ava Black
characters.description: Ava is a 30-year-old nurse who is emotionally fragile and resistant to acknowledging her need for help. She is conflicted about her past and the current situation with her family.; Around 30 / Female / Patient, 30 years old; Occupation: Nurse; Personality: Conflicted, Resistant, Emotionally Fragile; Values: Autonomy, Honesty, Self-awareness; Interests: Self-reflection, Emotional Healing, Family Relationships; Experiences: Failed marriage, Mental health issues, Family therapy discussions, Emotional suppression, Personal awakening

characters.name: Lora Black
characters.description: Ava's mother, Lora, is a 55-year-old retired teacher who is deeply concerned about Ava's well-being. She is patient but firm in her belief that professional help is necessary; Female; Age: 55; Occupation: Retired high school English teacher; Personality: Compassionate, analytical, resolute; Values: Family well-being, open communication, personal growth; Interests: Reading literary fiction, gardening, journaling; Experiences: Witnessed a student struggle with undiagnosed mental health issues, cared for a parent with chronic illness, supported Ava through a difficult adolescence.

characters.name: Amy Black
characters.description: Amy Black; Female; Age: 22; Occupation: Psychology student at a local university; Personality: Empathetic, diplomatic, observant, supportive, cautious; Values: Family harmony, emotional well-being, fairness; Interests: Reading self-help books, journaling, volunteering at a community mental health center; Experiences: Mediated conflicts between family members during childhood, witnessed Ava's struggles with anxiety, has personal experience with grief after the loss of a close friend.

actions.dialogue: Ava, I know this is hard for you, but you've been withdrawn and exhausted for months. I think it's time you see a therapist.
I don't need a therapist, Mom. I just need time to heal from my marriage. It's not about me—it's about what he did to me.

actions.action: Attempts to mediate and validate both sides
actions.dialogue: I understand, Ava. But maybe talking to someone could help you process it all. Mom just wants to see you better.
It's not that simple. I don't want to be seen as broken. I can handle this on my own, thank you.
I'm not saying you're broken, Ava. I'm saying you're hurting, and it's okay to ask for help. You don't have to do it alone.

scenes.plot: The family is trying to encourage Ava to seek professional help for her mental health, but she resists, attributing her pain to her failed marriage and not to any personal psychological issues. Amy tries to mediate, showing her understanding of both sides. The tension is palpable as Ava's emotional fragility and resistance to vulnerability come to the surface.
scenes.social_purpose: To explore the complexities of mental health discussions within a family, and how personal trauma can influence one's willingness to accept support.

chunk.text: The family's afternoon coffee meeting turns into a difficult but necessary conversation about Ava's emotional state. Each character's perspective is shaped by their values and experiences, highlighting the challenges of navigating personal pain and family expectations.
